name: nurt
description:
Danaco Nurt (`nurt`) — console for files, text, programs and the system (replaces bash and PowerShell; identical on Linux, macOS and Windows). Call parameter: `program` (Nurt text).

PROGRAM
program = [let name = PIPELINE]… PIPELINE. PIPELINE = source |> stage |> stage… A line ends a command; a line starting with `|>` continues it. Comment: `#`.
Data between stages are typed records (entry, line, match…), not text. `@name` = result of let; `...@name.path` = list spread. There is no $, cd, ;, &&, ||, -flags, text substitution or current directory.
Literals: path = quoted text "/srv/app" or "C:/proj" (always quoted, absolute, `/` separator; relative only with call parameter `base`); text "…" (escapes \\ \" \n \t \u{..}) or raw r"…" / r#"…"#; regex /…/i (flags i m s x; `\/` for slash; RE2 syntax); glob "**/*.go".
Also: size 10mb 1.5gib; duration 30s 5m 1h30m 7d; time "2026-11-21T10:00:00Z", ago(7d), now(); range 5, 1..5, 40.., ..9; list [a, b]; map {k: "v"}; document key "a.b[0].c".
Arguments: positional first, then `name: value`. Enum values are bare words (order: desc).
Expressions (filter, assert, select): record fields, == != < <= > >= ~ (regex) !~ in and or not + - * /, functions lower upper len trim contains(a,b) starts_with(a,b) ends_with(a,b) ago(d) now().

CONSTRUCTS
when COND { … } otherwise when COND { … } otherwise { … } — one branch runs; COND is bool: == != < and or not, `exists "/p"`, `(find "/d" |> count) > 0`, `exit_code`.
each (find "/d" glob: "*.log") as f { remove f.path } — the block runs per record in order (f.path, f.name); options parallel: N, atomic: false.
repeat until: COND every: 5s limit: 2m { … } runs, then tests (E_LIMIT if never met); while COND limit: 20 { … } tests first and ends normally at the limit; default loop.max_iterations 10000, loop.max_time 10m; break, continue.
steps { PIPELINE … } — several changes in one call, one per line; let passes results on. All or nothing; one undo reverses all.
define name(dir: path, keep: int = 7) { … } then name("/x", keep: 14) — typed parameters with defaults; the body sees only its parameters (@dir); the last statement is the result; recursion up to function.max_depth 64.
params { dir: path  days: int = 30  dry: bool = false } first in a file: `nurt run f.nurt dir: "/x" dry`. A bool without a value is true (remove preview); false is written out.
Each construct is one journal entry, typed before any effect; preview: true shows the branch and every iteration.

RULES
1. One action per step: at most one changing stage (write, replace, remove, move, copy, run…), placed last. It may be followed by verify (…), and after the effect by assert, filter, select, first, last, skip, count and sort on the result records. A failed check after the effect is an error without rollback; only verify rolls back. Several actions = several calls.
2. Patterns are allowed; the console lists the targets it computed. Optional check: assert count: 12 | paths: 12 | exit_code: 0.
3. The result shows the effect: diff, files, counts, sizes, notable (outside project, mass delete…) and irreversible. A changing stage on an empty list does nothing (0).
4. An error before the effect stops the whole program and nothing is changed. Files are written atomically with an etag check (E_STALE); encoding and line endings are preserved; output is UTF-8.
5. A write that adds a NEW syntax error to a known format (JSON, TOML, YAML, XML, code) is rolled back (validate: reject).
6. The form is corrected when safe (typos, units, quotes, bash and PowerShell habits); the result has `corrected` and `ran` (what was executed). If a correction would touch the target of a change, the answer is E_AMBIGUOUS with ready programs to resend.
7. A mistake visible in the result can be repaired with undo (history lists the operations; history state: partial and undo on_conflict: partial concern entries that can be restored only in part; undo paths: restores selected paths). It repairs errors and does not replace checking: use preview: true or assert when unsure.
8. Limits: the console does not prevent logic errors of the programs you run; changes made by run are detected only under `watch` (default: the working directory of the program) and may be marked irreversible.

CORE COMMANDS (UPPER = positional, * = required, … = list; name:value = default; name:a|b = enumeration, default first; name: = no default)

RECORDS (fields): entry(path name stem extension parent type size modified created mode owner link_target encoding line_ending binary hash etag) · content(path text lines etag encoding line_ending) · line(path no text) · match(path no column text line groups) · exec(command cwd exit_code signal timed_out stdout stderr changes) · job(id state exit_code elapsed stdout stderr) · operation(id time kind summary state files irreversible)

CALL PARAMETERS: preview (only targets and effect), base (directory for relative paths), limit=50, cursor, fields, format=text|json|markdown|compact, verbosity=quiet|normal|detailed, diff=none|stat|unified, max_chars, save_to, timeout, session, language.
A shortened result ends with `more: next`; call `next` for the next part.

EXAMPLES
find "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> filter size > 1mb |> sort size order: desc |> first 20
search /oldName\(/ "/srv/app/src" glob: "**/*.go" |> assert paths: 12 |> replace "newName("
find "/srv/app/build" glob: "**/*.tmp" |> remove
write "/srv/app/.gitignore" "dist/\n" mode: append
read "/srv/app/main.go" lines: 10..40
run ["go","test","./..."] cwd: "/srv/app" |> assert exit_code: 0
let ts = find "/srv/app" glob: "**/*.ts" |> filter modified > ago(1h)
@ts |> count

Groups (described on request with help group: NAME):
documents — Structured documents by key and SQLite databases.
text — Differences, patches, hashes, encodings, expressions and record operations.
code — Source code symbols, definitions, references, diagnostics, renaming and repository profile.
notebook — Cells of Jupyter notebooks.
git — Git repositories.
archive — Archives and compression.
system — Processes, ports, disks, host, environment, system logs and suspension of processes.
administration — System services, the registry provider, CIM, the firewall, routes, DNS and the clock.
package — System package managers.
network — HTTP requests, downloads, name resolution, ping and network interfaces.
schedule — Schedules of pipelines.
journal — Management of the journal, its space, limits, state and pinned entries.
program — Programs installed in the system: lookup, search, navigation and descriptions.
verify — Tests and code analysis through typed wrappers of test frameworks and analyzers.

Help: help, help "commands" (every command), help search: "words", help group: "documents", help "E_ASSERT", help skill: "bash-migration". Help is optional; it is never required before running a program.

program.description: Program text in any notation variant.

ast.description: Surface syntax tree nurt-ast/1, equivalent to program.

cursor.description: Cursor of a further page of an earlier result.

accept.description: Identifier of a candidate from an earlier E_AMBIGUOUS error.

preview.description: Only compute targets and effect; change nothing.

base.description: Absolute directory against which relative paths are resolved.

fields.description: Fields of the result to keep.

max_chars.description: Largest number of characters of a single text field; 0 means no limit.

save_to.description: Absolute path of a file that receives the full result instead of the response.

timeout.description: Time limit of the whole program.

session.description: Session identifier recorded in the journal.

script.description: Script mode: several pipelines, each its own operation.

privilege.description: Rights of the operation: the account, the administrator, or the account with one elevated repetition after E_PERMISSION or E_PRIVILEGE.

as_user.description: Account that runs the operation (Linux and macOS); implies elevation for the switch.
